findings.title: Cancellation during staged-output verification still publishes the file
findings.trigger: Cancel the worker while openInputStream(uri)/StreamIntegrity.fingerprint is reading a large staged destination, after the ensureActive at line146 and before rename/update starts.
findings.evidence: The fingerprint read is synchronous and checks Thread.isInterrupted, while ordinary Job.cancel does not interrupt a Dispatchers.IO thread. After fingerprint returns, save sets verified, writes the receipt and invokes publishVerified with no further coroutine cancellation check. Publication therefore begins after the user already cancelled; onCommitted sets terminal COMPLETE and TransferProcessor deliberately retains that state. This is a pre-commit cancellation, unlike the existing test which cancels from afterRename. It can cause a large verification read to finish and publish a download the user cancelled before publication.
findings.recommendation: Check currentCoroutineContext().ensureActive() after destination fingerprint validation and before setting verified/starting publication. Add a provider fixture that blocks the verification read, cancels the worker, releases the read, and asserts no rename or completed callback occurs.
findings.confidence: Source-proven conditional control-flow defect; no device execution. The missing cancellation checkpoint predates the current callback diff but remains exposed by this integration.

findings.title: A post-commit reopen failure is still reported as a failed download
findings.trigger: The provider successfully renames the verified document (or MediaStore clears IS_PENDING), the ready receipt is written, then the additional openFileDescriptor(finalUri, r) fails, for example because removable storage becomes unavailable at that point.
findings.evidence: PublicationReceipt.publish writes ready=true at lines161-162 before returning. OutputStore then performs another fallible provider open/stat at lines158-161 before notifying onCommitted at line164. If that open throws/returns null, verified=true preserves the published file, but TransferProcessor has never received the commit callback, so its terminal state remains CANCELLED and the exception path changes it to FAILED, records a failure, and acknowledges the queue. The cancellation fix only protects events after the callback; this path still labels an already committed download failed and halts the waiting queue.
findings.recommendation: Make the successful durable publication observable immediately at its commit boundary, and handle any subsequent availability check without converting the committed task into FAILED. Add a fault-provider test that succeeds at rename and fails only the next final-URI read.
findings.confidence: Source-proven conditional control-flow defect; no device execution. The final reopen predates this diff; the newly added commit callback is positioned after it.
